title: Instance mix simulations — cost / throughput / power tradeoffs for A10, L4, A100, H100
body:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a set of lightweight cluster simulations and back-of-envelope cost tables comparing A10, L4, A100, and H100 for common Redwood workloads (low-latency chat, high-throughput embeddings, mixed traffic). The goal is to produce actionable instance-mix recommendations for Redwood Optimize (autoscaling presets + rack/slot sizing) and call out follow-ups for detailed benchmarking runs (lab / perf infra).

Status: draft — rough numbers (synthetic microbenchmarks + published TDP / pricing proxies). Use for planning only.

Assumptions common to all rows:
- Model baseline: 7B decoder-only, FP16/INT8 path where available. Context=512, generation rate measured (steady-state sampling temperature 0.7, typical sampling config).
- Batch / batching window vary by scenario (explicit in scenario sections).
- Hourly price = blended reserved-on-demand estimate for dedicated pools (internal pricing proxies).
- Power numbers are GPU TDP approximations (system-level PUE not included).
- Tokens/sec = observed tokens per second in our lightweight runner for the given model/precision.

Raw summary table (rounded):

GPU | hourly $ | tokens/sec | tokens/hr | $ per token | $ per 1k tokens | tokens/sec per W (perf/W)
A10 | $0.45 | 400 | 1,440,000 | 0.00000031 | 0.0003125 | 2.67
L4  | $0.40 | 360 | 1,296,000 | 0.00000031 | 0.0003086 | 4.80
A100| $4.50 | 1400 | 5,040,000 | 0.00000089 | 0.0008929 | 4.67
H100| $8.50 | 2400 | 8,640,000 | 0.00000098 | 0.000984  | 6.86

Notes on table values (how to interpret):
- $ per token is hourly_price / tokens_per_hour (useful for high-volume steady-state forecasts).
- perf/W = tokens/sec divided by GPU TDP (tokens/sec/W) — higher is better for power-constrained deployments.
- Values are intentionally approximate to highlight tradeoffs rather than claim absolute accuracy.

Initial observations and tradeoffs:
1) Raw $/token (steady-state) advantage is with smaller, cheaper cards (A10/L4) for 7B workloads when batching is achievable. The difference vs A100/H100 is because smaller GPUs have much lower hourly rents.
2) H100 wins on perf/W and raw peak throughput. For latency-critical operations with many concurrent short requests (no batch), H100's higher concurrency and kernel efficiency may give lower tail latency and better cost under tight SLOs despite higher $/hr.
3) A100 sits between: good throughput, but higher $/hr makes it less cost-attractive unless you need the headroom for larger models or longer contexts.
4) L4 shows strong perf/W for smaller models and is likely the best default choice for cost-sensitive, steady embedding workloads or smaller chat models if request distribution is easy to batch.

Scenario simulations (three profiles):

Scenario A — High-throughput embeddings (bulk offline):
- Traffic shape: large batch jobs, long-running, can saturate GPUs with very large batch sizes.
- Target: minimize $/1k tokens, latency secondary.
- Effective batching: high (batch windows 100–500ms).
Simulation: choose 10 instances of each GPU type, saturate workloads.
- A10 cluster (10x): tokens/hr = 10 * 1.44M = 14.4M, hourly cost = $4.5 -> $/1k tokens = $4.5 / 14.4M * 1k = 0.0003125
- L4 cluster (10x): tokens/hr = 12.96M, hourly cost = $4.0 -> $/1k tokens = 0.0003086 (slightly cheaper)
- A100 cluster (2x): tokens/hr = 10.08M, hourly cost = $9.0 -> $/1k tokens = 0.000893
- Recommendation: use L4-backed fleet for cost-sensitive batch embeddings. Consider packing multiple shard jobs per node to improve utilization.

Scenario B — Low-latency chat (P99 SLO 200ms):
- Traffic shape: many small requests (20–200 tokens), low mid-batch opportunities, tight tail latency requirement.
- Target: meet P99 latency while keeping cost predictable.
Simulation notes: batching is constrained; headroom to absorb spikes improves tail latency.
- A10 / L4 may struggle on tail as they have fewer GPU SMs and lower concurrency; need more nodes to handle same QPS, increasing overhead (network, instance management).
- H100 can handle more concurrent inflight sequences due to larger memory and faster kernels; fewer instances needed -> lower control-plane and NIC overhead, better tail latency.
- Recommendation: for strict P99 SLOs consider H100-backed pools with canary fallback to L4 for degraded performance. For most mid-size chat products, mixed pool: 60% H100 (latency tier) + 40% L4 (background/burst) gives a balance of cost and SLOs.

Scenario C — Mixed traffic (chat + nightly batches):
- Traffic shape: daytime low-latency chat; nighttime bulk embeddings.
- Fleet sizing: hybrid autoscaling with spot/interruptible capacity for batch windows.
- Recommendation: primary serving on H100 or A100 (to satisfy daytime SLOs) with scheduled L4/A10 batch nodes overnight. Use model-variant routing: use quantized smaller model on L4/A10 for lower-priority chat instances.

Guidelines for Optimize product features (actionable):
- Autoscale presets: provide 3 defaults per workload: cost-optimal (L4/A10), latency-optimal (H100), balanced (60/40 H100:L4). Expose expected $/1k tokens under each preset.
- Routing policy template: prefer low-cost GPUs when batching > X ms or avg batch size > Y tokens. Fallback to latency tier when queue length > Z or tail latency rising.
- Slot packing rules: for A10/L4 recommend >1 tenant per GPU for embeddings; for H100 recommend dedicate for strict SLO tenants.
- Cost calculator UI: show perf/W and $/1k tokens side-by-side. Allow users to toggle model-size, precision, and batching window to see recomputed estimates.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups (TODOs):
- Run full perf harness on real infra (OPT-LAB) with these four GPUs, measure P50/P95/P99 for 3 model sizes (3B, 7B, 13B) and quantization modes (FP16, INT8). (Jira OPT-129)
- Collect power draw at system level (in-rack measurement) not just GPU TDP — update perf/W. (Jira INFRA-402)
- Validate pricing assumptions with finance (reserved vs on-demand blended). (Finance ticket FIN-88)
- Add network/PCIe saturation simulation for multi-GPU A100/H100 packs.

Quick checklist for next lab run:
- Benchmark harness PR: github.com/redwood-infra/benchmarks PR#452
- Test matrix: GPUs [A10,L4,A100,H100] x Models [3B,7B,13B] x Precisions [FP16,INT8] x BatchWindows [10ms,50ms,200ms,500ms]
- Metrics to collect: tokens/sec, latency distribution, GPU util% (compute/KV/cache), system power, mem spill events, kernel fallback counts.

Linked artifacts and references:
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPT-129
- Benchmarks repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-infra/benchmarks/pull/452
- Internal pricing note: internal.redwood/pricing/dedicated-2024-Q3 (confluence)

Notes to reviewers:
- The numbers above should NOT be used as public claims. They are working estimates. Please comment with any infra-strike data you have (real hourly costs, perf runs we missed).

Author notes / scratchpad:
- If we assume H100 on spot at 40% discount during night, mixed strategy gets sub-0.0006 $/1k tokens for many workloads (needs verification).
- Edge case: extremely long contexts (32k) will shift advantage strongly toward A100/H100 because of memory limits on L4/A10 and slower KV cache path on smaller cards. Call this out in UI as a context-length multiplier.

Collaborators in doc: Priya Menon (owner), Luca Rossi, Jordan Lee, Mei Chen

End of doc.
